description: Which implementation-guide packages scripts/interop/fhir-validate.sh loads for each golden in conformance/golden/. The profile itself is NOT listed here: every instance declares its own in meta.profile, and the validator resolves it out of the packages named below. A golden with no packages is validated against base FHIR R4 only, which is weaker on purpose and recorded as such.

prior-authorization-eob.note: Declares the PDex Prior Authorization profile. This is the Patient Access prior-authorization payload CMS-0057-F asks for.

claim-eob.note: The Patient Access EOB for an 837P, on the CARIN BB Professional NonClinician profile — the financial half of the family, so it carries the adjudication amounts and the total set the Basis profiles forbid.

carin-inpatient-financial.note: The same claim type as carin-inpatient-basis on the financial profile: everything the Basis profile requires, plus the money.

carin-outpatient-financial.note: The outpatient bill classification on the financial profile.

carin-oral-financial.note: An 837D on the Oral profile, which requires two adjudication entries per line as the professional profile does.

carin-professional-basis.note: The Provider Access payload for an 837P, on the CARIN BB Professional NonClinician Basis profile. Non-financial by requirement, not by simplification: the Basis family exists so a payer can send another provider the record of an encounter without the plan's financial terms.

carin-inpatient-basis.note: An 837I whose type of bill says inpatient. This profile asks for more than the others: an admission period and a revenue code on every line.

carin-outpatient-basis.note: The same 837I with an outpatient bill classification, which selects a different profile with a different diagnosis-type value set.

carin-oral-basis.note: An 837D on the Oral Basis profile, which is the strictest of the four on network status: it requires a rendering network status CHO can only supply once the claim has been adjudicated on a mappable tier.

claim-as-billed.note: Base R4 only. A FHIR Claim is CHO-native source material, not a payload any CMS-0057-F profile governs, so there is no IG to load.

encounter.note: Base R4 only, for the same reason as claim-as-billed. Provider Access carries encounters inside a non-financial ExplanationOfBenefit, not as FHIR Encounter.
